_readme: HANDOVER for the user's AI. Paste this whole file into the AI, then describe the site/page you want. Follow `site_brief` (folder-based). Everything after it is reference.

framework.name: Viewscape One
framework.what_it_is: A static, build-free, GitHub-Pages-ready framework. The home page is a field of tiles; each tile is a folder under pages/<source>/<slug>/ (sources: 'me' and 'ai'). Opening a tile loads that page in a holographic box; branded pages also get a radial 'weapon wheel' on the right edge. A page can be hand/AI-built HTML/CSS/JS (custom) or a JSON-driven data page.
framework.philosophy: Show data neatly. Prefer few strong sections over many weak ones. Lead with a summary, then stats/charts, then detail tables, then sources. Write real, specific content. Never invent facts presented as real: label fictional or estimated numbers.
framework.stack: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. No build step, no npm packages needed at runtime.

site_brief._note: PRIMARY TASK. The user's AI builds whole pages/sites as FOLDERS. Output = a folder of files the user drops into pages/ai/<slug>/ . (The JSON data-page + bundle system further down is an optional shortcut; ignore it unless asked.)
site_brief.deliverable: One folder: pages/ai/<slug>/ containing index.html (entry) + any css/js/images/video/data files it needs. Then ONE line is added to pages/ai/index.json: the slug. That is the entire installation.
site_brief.page_json_required: Also create pages/ai/<slug>/page.json (metadata for the home tile): {"type":"custom","title":"…","subtitle":"one-line hook","description":"…","icon":"chart","accent":"magenta|red|violet|turquoise|sky|mint","tags":["a","b"],"author":"ai","updated":"YYYY-MM-DD", "entry":"index.html"(optional), "cover":"cover.jpg"(optional)}. Icons: see icons list below.
site_brief.how_the_page_is_shown: The page loads inside a holographic iframe box on the home field (and also works standalone). It can be ANY site: vanilla, React/Vite build output, three.js, a game, a dashboard, a separate framework. Use RELATIVE paths only (GitHub Pages sub-path hosting). No build step may be required at runtime — commit built output.

two_modes.A_branded (recommended): Include the Viewscape scripts so the page gets the same look + the radial wheel. Copy templates/custom/index.html as the starting point (it links ../../../assets/css/*.css and ../../../assets/js/*.js and has <body data-vs-page data-vs-mode="custom">). Mark jump targets with data-vs-section="Label". Style with the theme tokens. Reuse blocks via VS.blocks.render([...], element).
two_modes.B_independent: Fully standalone site, no Viewscape files. It still appears on the field and loads in the hologram box. Optional: add a back button that calls parent.postMessage({vs:'close'},'*'), and open other Viewscape pages with parent.postMessage({vs:'open',ref:'me/welcome'},'*').

site_brief.style_tokens: CSS vars from assets/css/theme.css: --vs-bg #05030a, --vs-ink, --vs-dim, --accent / --accent-rgb / --accent2, palette --vs-mag #ff2bd6 --vs-red #ff2a55 --vs-vio #9b6bff --vs-tur #2ef2e0 --vs-sky #9fd8ff --vs-mint #a8ffd0; fonts --f-disp (Orbitron) --f-body (Rajdhani) --f-mono (Share Tech Mono). Helpers: class vs-glass (liquid glass panel), vs-btn, vs-chip, vs-tag, vs-title, vs-eyebrow, vs-card, vs-holoframe (hologram corners), data-reveal (scroll-in). Aesthetic: black base, magenta/red primary, small violet/turquoise/baby-blue/mint accents, Iron-Man holographic HUD + Apple liquid glass + retro-tech.
site_brief.wheel_for_custom_pages: Add page-specific wedges in page.json: "wheel":{"label":"Tools","extras":[{"label":"Reset","icon":"zap","action":{"type":"event","name":"my:reset"}}]} and listen with document.addEventListener('my:reset', …). Actions: page, link, url, scroll, copy, accent, event.
site_brief.media_and_links: Videos: <video src="clip.mp4" controls> or YouTube/Vimeo iframes. Multiple paragraphs, images, files: plain HTML. Link to other Viewscape pages with VS.nav.open('me/welcome') (branded mode) or the postMessage above; link to files with relative hrefs.
checklist: Folder name = slug ([a-z0-9-], <=48 chars) and listed in pages/ai/index.json.
index.html opens correctly from its own folder.
All paths relative; no leading slash; no localhost URLs.
If using the Viewscape scripts the relative depth is exactly ../../../assets/ .
Mobile friendly: leave ~4.5rem of right padding on small screens so the wheel orb doesn't cover content (class vs-wrap does this).
site_brief.reply_format: Return the files as separate code blocks, each preceded by its full path (e.g. pages/ai/my-site/index.html). Do not wrap in JSON.

folder_structure.viewscape.config.json: Names the SOURCE folders (who owns pages): e.g. 'me' and 'ai'. AI always uses source 'ai' unless told otherwise.
folder_structure.assets/: The framework library (css/ js/). NEVER edit or copy it into a page.
folder_structure.pages/<source>/index.json: The list of page slugs shown on the home field for that source.
folder_structure.pages/<source>/<slug>/: One page. Contains page.json (+ index.html) and any media/data files it needs.
folder_structure.templates/: page/ (data page) and custom/ (hand-built page) starters used by the CLI and Studio.
folder_structure.studio/: In-browser tool: paste a bundle, preview it, download a zip.
folder_structure.tools/vs.mjs: CLI: new / remove / hide / show / import / validate / serve.

output_contract.instruction: Return ONE JSON object (no markdown fences, no commentary) in this shape. For several pages return a JSON array of such objects.

files.optional/relative/path.json: string content, or a JSON object (it will be stringified). Use for data files referenced by blocks via `src`.

rules: Paths inside blocks (src, href, image...) are RELATIVE to the page folder, e.g. "data/sales.json". Never use absolute paths or leading slashes.
Binary media (images/videos) cannot be in the bundle: reference files the user will add (state the filenames in a callout block) or use https:// URLs / YouTube / Vimeo links.
Valid JSON only: double quotes, no comments, no trailing commas.
Put the finished date in page.updated as YYYY-MM-DD.
Do not include `entry` unless you are making a custom page.

fields.title: string — shown on tile + page header
fields.subtitle: string — one-line hook (tile + header). Keep < 90 chars.
fields.description: string — a short paragraph. Markdown-lite allowed.
fields.icon: icon name (see icons) OR a single emoji/glyph
fields.accent: magenta | red | violet | turquoise | sky | mint  (default magenta)
fields.tags: array of short strings (max 3 shown on tile)
fields.author: 'ai' or 'me'
fields.cover: optional image/video path (relative) for tile + header background

wheel.label: name of the extras sub-wheel
wheel.extras: array (max 8) of { label, icon, hint?, action }  — extra wedges for this page

fields.sections: array of { id?, title, description?, icon?, blocks: [...] } — each section becomes a numbered chapter AND a wheel jump-target

wheel_actions.page: { "type":"page", "ref":"ai/other-slug" }  open another page in the hologram

text_formatting.page_link: [[source/slug|label]] opens another Viewscape page inside the hologram.
text_formatting.paragraphs: Use block `text` with `paragraphs: ["p1","p2"]` OR one `text` string with blank lines between paragraphs (also supports # headings, - lists, 1. lists, > quotes, ``` code fences). A bare string inside `blocks` is shorthand for a paragraph.

blocks._note: Every block is { "type": "…", …props, accent?, label?, id? }. `label` adds a small eyebrow above it. Blocks whose data is large can use `src` pointing to a JSON file (ship it in `files`).

hero.props: title, subtitle?, eyebrow?, tags[]?, image?|video?, cta[{label,href|page,ghost?}]?

callout.use: key takeaway, warning, caveats, 'files to add'

stats.use: headline KPIs; numeric `value` count-up animates; `delta` starting with '-' shows red

chart.props: kind(bar|line|area|donut|radar|spark), title?, data, caption?, height?, multicolor?, centerLabel?
chart.guidance: bar=compare categories · line/area=trend over time · donut=parts of a whole (<=6 slices) · radar=profile on 3-8 axes · spark=tiny trend

table.props: columns[] , rows[][] | rows[{col:value}], caption?, search?(default on if >6 rows)
table.note: sortable, filterable; numbers auto-format; cells accept inline markdown

links.use: navigation cards to other pages (page:'source/slug') or files/URLs

video.props: src, caption?, poster?, ratio?('16/9'), autoplay?, loop?, muted?
video.note: src may be a relative .mp4/.webm OR a YouTube/Vimeo URL (auto-embeds)

embed.note: iframe; only https sites that allow embedding

md.use: load a markdown file from the page folder (ship it in `files`)

include.use: pull blocks from another JSON file (array of blocks, or {blocks}/{sections})

tabs.use: alternate views of the same topic

design_guidance: Section 1 = 'Summary' with a callout (key finding) + 3-4 stats.
Use 3-6 sections. Give each a short `title` and an `icon` — they become wheel wedges.
Pick ONE accent per page that fits the topic (magenta/red = intense, turquoise = tech/data, violet = abstract/creative, sky = calm, mint = growth/health).
Every chart gets a `title`. Keep labels short (<12 chars).
Write multiple real paragraphs where explanation is needed; don't cram prose into stats or tables.
Always finish with a 'Sources & notes' section (links block or list) when data is real.
If numbers are illustrative say so in a callout (tone: warn).

new_page_by_ai_data_bundle: User gives a topic and (optionally) data.
AI returns the bundle JSON (see output_contract).
User opens /studio/ → paste → Validate → Download zip → drop zip contents into the repo root (merge), or run: node tools/vs.mjs import bundle.json
Commit + push. The tile appears on the home field.
workflows.update_existing_page: Return the same slug with the full new `page`. Import with --overwrite (Studio does this automatically).
remove_page: node tools/vs.mjs hide <source> <slug>           (keeps files, hides from field)
No CLI? Delete pages/<source>/<slug>/ and remove the slug from pages/<source>/index.json.
add_page_manually: node tools/vs.mjs new <source> <slug> --title "My Page"   (add --custom for your own HTML/CSS/JS)
Or copy templates/page → pages/<source>/<slug>/ and add the slug to pages/<source>/index.json.
workflows.add_a_source_folder: node tools/vs.mjs source add <id> --label "Name" --icon bot --accent violet
workflows.custom_or_separate_framework_page: Set page.json "type":"custom" and use any index.html/css/js (or a whole third-party framework build) inside the page folder. Optional `entry` in page.json names the HTML file. Include the Viewscape scripts (see templates/custom/index.html) to get the wheel + ambience; omit them for a totally independent page — it still appears on the field and loads in the hologram box.

page_types.data: page.json drives everything (default, preferred for AI).
page_types.custom: page.json has only metadata (title, subtitle, icon, accent, tags, wheel…). The folder owns index.html + page.css + page.js. Use VS.blocks.render([...], el) to reuse library blocks.

quality_checklist: page.title and at least one section with blocks.
All block types come from the list above. Charts have numeric data.
No absolute/leading-slash paths. No <script> in html blocks.
Sections have titles (wheel labels) and icons from the icon list.

page.title: Coffee Brief
page.subtitle: Where the world's coffee comes from.
page.author: ai

blocks.title: Key finding
blocks.text: Three countries grow over half of the world's coffee.

paragraphs: Coffee is grown in a belt around the equator.
Brazil alone supplies roughly a third of the world's beans.

start_prompt_for_user: Paste HANDOVER.json, then: "Build a Viewscape One page called <NAME> about <TOPIC>. Mode A (branded). Accent <colour>. It should <what it must show/do>. Reply with each file in its own code block with its full path."
